summary: A short elevated public garden on the former rail viaduct between traffic lanes of Phra Pok Klao Bridge, giving river and old-city views between Phra Nakhon and Thonburi.
whyGo: Get a distinctive view from above the Chao Phraya, including the Memorial Bridge and riverfront neighborhoods.
Walk a compact 280 m landscaped path with three viewing platforms, then continue to the flower market or nearby riverside temples.
bestFor: A free, short stop for river views and photography.
Walkers combining the old town, Pak Khlong Talat, and the Thonburi riverfront.
skipIf: You want a quiet nature escape: the park is elevated between active road lanes, so traffic noise and vehicle emissions are part of the setting.
You need extensive shaded seating, toilets, or indoor facilities; the official listing does not promise these amenities.
duration: Allow about 20–40 minutes for the short out-and-back walk and viewpoints; this is a planning estimate, not a venue limit.
cost: Free admission according to Greener Bangkok. Budget separately for transit or a taxi.
hours: Greener Bangkok and the Tourism Authority of Thailand list daily hours as 05:00–20:00. Recheck locally before visiting in December 2026 in case of temporary closures.
bestTime: Go near sunrise or late afternoon for softer light and cooler temperatures; confirm the gate is open within the published hours. Midday can feel exposed.
gettingThere: The Bangkok city park listing gives MRT Sanam Chai as the nearest rail access; continue on foot toward Phra Pok Klao Bridge and follow map directions to the park entrance. City bus routes 3, 7ก, 9, 42, 8, 73, 73ก and 82 are also listed. A 2020 BMA notice mentions Chao Phraya Express Boat orange-flag and ordinary boats at Saphan Phut pier; verify current pier service and routes before relying on it. The path connects both riverbanks.
booking: No booking is indicated; this is a free public park. Check BMA updates for closures or special restrictions.
accessibility: Greener Bangkok lists lifts for disabled visitors and older people, plus the 280 m pedestrian/cycling route. Lift operation, step-free approach details, and access during maintenance are not confirmed; check on arrival. The route is elevated, and assistance may be useful for visitors who are uneasy with height or traffic noise.
practicalTips: Use the official map pin and check which side entrance is most convenient; the park sits in the center of the bridge rather than at street level.
Wear comfortable shoes and bring water; there is limited room to shelter if weather turns.
Cycling is listed as an activity, so keep to the appropriate side and watch for other users.
BMA rules prohibit drones, smoking, alcohol, gambling, and damaging plants.
decemberNotes: December is generally a more comfortable time for outdoor walking in Bangkok, but daytime sun remains strong. For a December 2026 visit, check the city listing and transit services close to the day; no special December 2026 event or closure notice was found.
uncertainties: Operating hours and admission are currently listed by BMA and TAT, but December 2026 maintenance or temporary closures are unknown.
The BMA bus/ferry information is from a 2020 opening notice; routes, piers, and service frequencies may have changed.
The official listing notes lifts but does not specify wheelchair dimensions, lift status, restrooms, shade coverage, or other access details.
